edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Because S. boulardii survives antibacterial therapy and supports barrier function, it is a plausible countermeasure against antibiotic-associated diarrhea.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2018 McFarland meta analysis in Front Med (Lausanne), which suggests that saccharomyces boulardii tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
